L27: # Functional English
L28: 
L29: Page Content
L30: 
L31: ​​​​On 7 August 2025, the English language tests approved for Australian visa purposes changed. If you took a test before this date, your result may still be valid as proof of functional English for up to 12 months, depending on the 【4†visa subclass】.
L32: 
L33: To prove you have functional English, show us evidence of one of the following:
L34:   * You are a citizen of, and hold a valid passport issued by, one of the following countries:
L35:     * Canada
L36:     * New Zealand
L37:     * The Republic of Ireland
L38:     * The United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
L39:     * The United States of America.
L40:   * You completed a degree, a higher degree, a diploma or a trade certificate in an institution in or outside Australia that required at least 2 years of full-time study or training, and all instructions were in English.
L41:   * You completed education at the institutions for the study times set out at Table 1.
L42:   * You achieved one of the test scores in Table 2 or Table 3 in the 12 months before your visa application.
L43: Table 1 - Functional English education institutions and study time
L44: Educational institutions  | ​Study time
L45: --- | ---
L46: A primary school and secondary school, in or outside Australia, where all instruction was in English  | All years of primary and at least 3 years of secondary education
L47: A secondary school, in or outside Australia, where all instruction was in English  | At least 5 years of secondary education
L48: An institution in Australia, where all instruction was in English, towards one of the following awards:
L49:   * a degree
L50:   * a higher degree
L51:   * a diploma
L52:   * an associate diploma.
L53:  |
L54: 
L55:   * At least 1 year of full-time study towards an award, or
L56:   * The part-time equivalent of 1 year of full-time study towards an award
L57: 
L58: ​
L59: ​ ​ ​Table 2 - Functional English approved tests and scores taken on or after 7 August 2025​
L60: Test  | ​Scores
L61: --- | ---
L62: 【5†Canadian English Language Proficiency Index Program General (CELPIP General)†www.celpip.ca】  | An overall band score of at least 5
L63: 【6†International English Language Testing System (IELTS Academic)†ielts.org】
L64: The department accepts IELTS test results that include 【7†One Skill Retake​†ielts.org】 (OSR) for eligible visas. To find out if you are eligible, check the relevant 【4†visa page​】.  | An average band score of at least 4.5
L65: 【8†International English Language Testing System (IELTS General Training)†ielts.org】
L66: The department accepts IELTS test results that include 【7†One Skill Retake​†ielts.org】 (OSR) for eligible visas. To find out if you are eligible, check the relevant 【4†visa page​】.  | An average band score of at least 4.5
L67: 【9†Michigan English Test (MET)†michiganassessment.org】
L68: The department accepts MET test results that include 【10†Single Section Retake​†michiganassessment.org】 (SSR) for eligible visas. To find out if you are eligible, check the relevant 【4†visa page】.  | An overall band score of at least 38
L69: 【11†Occupational English Test (OET)†oet.com】
L70: This test is developed for health professionals. The OET scoring format was previously alphabetical and changed to numerical on 7 August 2025.
L71: OET does not currently provide 【12†overall test results†oet.com】 on test score reports. However, you can get your overall OET score results by contacting 【13†OET†oet.com】.  | An overall band score of at least 1020
L72: 【14†LANGUAGECERT Academic Test (LANGUAGECERT Academic)†www.languagecert.org】​​​  | An overall band score of at least 38
L73: 【15†Pearson Test of English Academic (PTE Academic)†www.pearsonpte.com】
L74: PTE Academic has the same name as the previous version of the test that was accepted before 7 August 2025.
L75: However, the test and scores are different.  | An overall band score of at least 24
L76: 【16†Test of English as a Foreign Language internet-Based Test (TOEFL iBT)†www.ets.org】
L77: To ensure your TOEFL iBT result is valid for Australian visa purposes, you must select ‘Taking TOEFL for Australia’ when registering for your test.
L78: Results not registered under this pathway may not be accepted for Australian visa purposes.  | A total score of at least 26
L79: ​ ​ Table 3 - Functional English approved tests and scores taken on or before 6 August 2025*
L80: Test  | ​Scores
L81: --- | ---
L82: 【17†Cambridge C1 Advanced Test (C1 Advanced)†www.cambridgeenglish.org】
L83: Previously known as Cambridge English: Advanced (CAE)​
L84: From 12 February 2024 to 6 August 2025, the department will only accept results from the Cambridge C1 Advanced paper-based test.
L85: The department will still accept tests taken before 12 February 2024 and within specified validity periods, for C1 Advanced paper-based and computer-based tests.  | A total band score of at least 147
L86: 【18†International English Language Testing System (IELTS Academic or General Training)​†ielts.org】​​
L87: From 14 December 2022, the department accepts IELTS test results that include 【7†One Skill Retake​†ielts.org】 (OSR) for eligible visas. To find out if you are eligible, check the relevant 【4†visa page】.  | An average band score of at least 4.5
L88: 【15†Pearson Test of English Academic (PTE Academic)​†www.pearsonpte.com】 PTE Academic has the same name as the test available from 7 August 2025, however, the test and scores are different.  | A total band score of at least 30
L89: 【16†Test of English as a Foreign Language internet-Based Test (TOEFL iBT)†www.ets.org】
L90: From 26 July 2023 to ​4 May 2024, the TOEFL iBT test was not approved for Australian visa purposes.  | A total band score of at least 32

L55: Part 1—Preliminary
L56: 
L57: 1  Name
L58:   This instrument is the Migration (Evidence of Functional English Language Proficiency) Instrument 2025.
L59: 
L60: 2  Commencement
L61: 
L62:   This instrument commences on 7 August 2025.
L63: 
L64: 3  Authority
L65: 
L66:   This instrument is made under paragraph 5.17(a) of the Migration Regulations 1994.
L67: 
L68: 4  Definitions
L69: 
L70:   In this instrument:
L71: 
L72: Act means the Migration Act 1958.
L73: 
L74: average band score means a test score calculated from the makeup of the scores received for each of the English test components.
L75: CELPIP General means the Canadian English Language Proficiency Index Program General.
L76: 
L77: English test components means all of the following:
L78: 
L79:  (a) listening;
L80: 
L81:  (b) reading;
L82: 
L83:  (c) speaking; and
L84: 
L85:  (d) writing.
L86: 
L87: IELTS Academic means the International English Language Test System Academic.
L88: 
L89: IELTS General Training means the International English Language Test System General Training.
L90: 
L91: LANGUAGECERT Academic means the LANGUAGECERT Academic Test.
L92: Language tests means the language tests mentioned in column 1 of the table in Schedule 1 to this instrument.
L93: 
L94: MET means the Michigan English Test.
L95: 
L96: OET means the Occupational English Test.
L97: 
L98: Overall band score means a test score calculated from the makeup of the scores received for each of the English test components.
L99: 
L100: PTE Academic means Pearson Test of English Academic.
L101: 
L102: relevant application means an application, including (but not limited to):
L103: 
L104:  (a) an application for a visa; or
L105:  (b) an application under section 140GB of the Act to approve a nomination under subsection 140GB(2) of the Act;
L106: 
L107: where a person is required, for the purposes of that application, to satisfy a criterion or meet a requirement under the Act or the Regulations to have functional English.
L108: 
L109: Note: For the meaning of functional English, see subsection 5(2) of the Act.
L110: Example 1: Subregulation 2.72A(14) of the Regulations provides that one of the criteria for the Minister to approve a nomination under subsection 140GB(2) of the Act is that the Minister is satisfied that the nominee has functional English.
L111: 
L112: Example 2: Under clause 407.212 of Schedule 2 to the Regulations, the applicant for a Subclass 407 (Training) visa must satisfy the Minister that the applicant has functional English.
L113: 
L114: Regulations means the Migration Regulations 1994.
L115: Minimum test scores means: see paragraph 6(3)(a) of this instrument.
L116: 
L117: TOEFL iBT means Test of English as a Foreign Language internet-Based Test.
L118: 
L119: Total band score means a test score calculated from the makeup of the scores received for each of the English test components.

L121: 5  Schedules
L122:   Each instrument that is specified in a Schedule to this instrument is amended or repealed as set out in the applicable items in the Schedule concerned, and any other item in a Schedule to this instrument has effect according to its terms.
L123: 
L124: Part 2—Specified evidence of English language proficiency
L125: 
L126: 6  Specified evidence of English language proficiency
L127:   For the purposes of paragraph 5(2)(b) of the Act, the following requirements are specified and recognised as prescribed evidence of the English language proficiency of a person who has functional English:
L128: 
L129:  (a) the person provides evidence of having completed one of the following at an educational institution or institutions in which all instruction was conducted in English:
L130: 
L131:  (i) all years of primary education and at least 3 years of secondary education; or
L132:  (ii) at least 5 years of secondary education; or
L133: 
L134:  (b) the person provides evidence of having successfully completed, in Australia, at least 1 year of full-time study or equivalent part-time study towards one or more of the following at an institution or institutions, where all the instruction was conducted in English:
L135: 
L136:  (i) a degree; or
L137: 
L138:  (ii) a higher degree; or
L139: 
L140:  (iii) a diploma; or
L141: 
L142:  (iv) an associate diploma; or
L143:  (c) the person provides evidence of having achieved one of the minimum test scores mentioned in column 2, 3 or 4 of the table in Schedule 1 in a test mentioned in column 1 of the same item of the table, and where:
L144: 
L145:  (i) that test was based on the English test components; and
L146: 
L147:  (ii) that test was undertaken:
L148: 
L149:  (A) in the period of 12 months immediately before the day on which the relevant application is made; or
L150: 
L151:  (B) on or after the day on which the relevant application is made; or
L152:  (d) the person provides evidence that they are a citizen of, and hold a valid passport issued by, one of the following countries:
L153: 
L154:  (i) Canada; or
L155: 
L156:  (ii) New Zealand; or
L157: 
L158:  (iii) the Republic of Ireland; or
L159: 
L160:  (iv) the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland; or
L161: 
L162:  (v) the United States of America.
L163: 
L164: 7  Specified evidence of English language proficiency—tests undertaken before commencement of this instrument
L165:  (1) For the purposes of paragraph 5(2)(b) of the Act, the requirements in subsections (2), (3), (4) and (5) are specified under subregulation 5.17(a) of the Regulations as prescribed evidence of the English language proficiency of a person, for the purposes of a relevant application:
L166: 
L167:  (a) that is made on or after the day this instrument commences; and
L168: 
L169:  (b) where the person has undertaken a test that is mentioned in any one of subsections (2), (3), (4) or (5), and where the test was undertaken:
